description: History, culture, and legacy of the Roman civilization

chronology.kingdom: 753–509 BCE; legendary founding by Romulus; seven kings
chronology.republic: 509–27 BCE; Senate and consuls; expansion across Mediterranean

government.senate: 300 patrician members; advised magistrates, controlled finances
government.consuls: Two elected annually; commanded armies, led senate
government.tribunes: Protected plebeian rights; could veto senate acts
government.dictator: Appointed in emergencies for max 6 months

roman_republic.expansion: Conquered Italian peninsula by 270 BCE, then Carthage, Greece, Spain, Gaul

punic_wars.second: 218–201 BCE; Hannibal crossed Alps; Rome defeated Carthage
punic_wars.third: 149–146 BCE; Carthage destroyed; Carthago delenda est

late_republic.marius: Military reforms; professional army loyal to general
late_republic.julius_caesar: Crossed Rubicon 49 BCE; dictator; assassinated Ides of March 44 BCE
late_republic.octavian: Won civil wars; became Augustus Caesar; end of Republic

roman_empire.augustus: First emperor (27 BCE–14 CE); Pax Romana began
roman_empire.pax_romana: 200 years of relative peace and prosperity (~27 BCE–180 CE)
roman_empire.crisis_of_third_century: 235–284 CE; 50+ emperors; civil wars, plague, economic collapse
roman_empire.constantine: First Christian emperor; Edict of Milan 313 CE; founded Constantinople 330 CE
roman_empire.theodosian_code: Christianity made official state religion 380 CE
roman_empire.fall_of_west: 476 CE; Romulus Augustulus deposed by Odoacer

culture_and_society.slavery: Up to 35% of population; foundation of Roman economy

religion.polytheistic: Roman gods (Jupiter, Juno, Mars, Venus, Mercury, etc.)

entertainment.colosseum: Built 70–80 CE; held 50,000–80,000 spectators; gladiatorial games

contributions_to_civilization.law: Roman law basis of most modern legal systems; 'Corpus Juris Civilis'
contributions_to_civilization.language: Latin evolved into Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Romanian
contributions_to_civilization.calendar: Julian calendar (45 BCE); basis of modern Gregorian calendar
contributions_to_civilization.roads: 80,000 km of paved roads; still partially in use
contributions_to_civilization.government: Concepts of republic, senate, and written law influence modern democracies
